subject.title: [Bug]: sessions_spawn child runs fail after acceptance with HTTP 401 Missing scopes api.responses.write

question: Should native `sessions_spawn` child runs inherit the parent session's effective runtime/auth-profile state by default, or should spawn fail before acceptance when the derived child route would require different OpenAI auth scopes?
rationale: The source gap is clear enough to keep the issue open, but the correct repair changes the runtime/auth ownership contract for child sessions and should be decided by the owner of agent session routing rather than inferred by cleanup automation.

options.title: Inherit parent runtime/auth by default
options.body: For same-agent child runs without an explicit incompatible route, copy the parent's effective runtime and auth-profile state into the child and add fail-fast validation for missing scopes.

options.title: Fail fast on divergent child auth
options.body: Keep child route selection separate but reject `sessions_spawn` before acceptance whenever the child route cannot prove the required OpenAI scope/profile.

options.title: Delegate to broader OAuth fallback work
options.body: Track only the missing OpenAI OAuth scope/fallback behavior in the related OAuth issue and explicitly document that child sessions do not inherit parent auth context.

recommendation.title: Inherit parent runtime/auth by default
recommendation.body: For same-agent child runs without an explicit incompatible route, copy the parent's effective runtime and auth-profile state into the child and add fail-fast validation for missing scopes.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame places the central native spawn planning and model-session persistence code under this recent area work, even though full history is shallow.
